items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: And then they hired Frank Keelan. Frank Keelan played trumpet. ... I played bass, you know. I'd taken Sam Orange's place on the bass.

ctx.x: a... a... Yeah. Well, I've been trying to think for three days of a trumpet player. I told Ralph the other day, it begins with K. from uptown. It went through my head. Keelan. Frank Keelan?

Frank Keelan was a trumpet player. With this one of these old... You know, like you ever heard him, I guess you would call it a barrel house. You know. That's a barrel house. That's a barrel house. That's a barrel house. Yeah. Well, he didn't play in all these good time, big time bands, you know. But all those bands like we were like... I had one time when we was playing up at Tom Anderson. When I worked at Tom Anderson, he played... He played trumpet in there, because he... It was... He played soft trumpet, you…

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: We had Frank Keelan playing trumpet with us then.

ctx.x: Well, you know, John Lawler told me a lot of boxers used to hang out by the, uh, Big 25.

Yeah. That was good. See, trying a long, long time ago, that's where they used to have all them big coach games, around 25. Frank Keelan was a trumpet player. He used to gamble at 25. And they had a big guy called Zack, Big, Big Zack, big black fella. Him and Frank Keelan got in a humbug, caught Frank messing around with a deck of cards,

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Who were some of the bad guys? Uh, Willi Peen, any Willi Peen, the Keelan brothers.

ctx.x: Well, I think I met that sister. I think her sister is a classical piano player. Rick Rita. I don't think she plays any jazz at all. So, the same one is to teach her? Yeah, I think that's the same one. One is to teach piano? Yeah, yeah, in Washington or something. She's one of the founders of the B-Sharp Music Club. Uh, did, uh, could you tell me where you were when the, uh, Robert Charles riot took place? Do you remember when they killed Robert Charles? Yeah. And he killed all those policemen?

I was, uh, uh, I lived on, uh, Benville Street and I believe I was, uh, that's about thirty, over thirty-five years now. Uh-huh. Yeah, I was living on Benville Street. My first wife would die just then. Uh-huh. Were you playing music then? Yeah, I was playing. Yeah. I was playing with Reddy then. Oh yeah? Yeah, with Robert Charles Wright, you know what? Sure. The mob came up for us, Claiborne and, uh, let's see, it was, uh, Claiborne and Borgias. Uh-huh. And we called, we had the, uh, the battlefield, was called…
Uh-huh. Not, not Frankie. Frank Keelan. The trumpet player?
